title: The Least Valuable Points in Basketball
dek: Once a game is decided the points do not come easier. They come slower and they count for less — and they still land in every average you read.
headline: Once a Q4 lead passes 15 points the leading team scores 105.34 per 100 possessions, against a 112.51 baseline for the same quarter — 7.17 points BELOW, not above. Shot quality is flat (48.77 eFG% vs 49.68 for a leader in a one-possession game); the entire gap is the free throws a close game manufactures. The least meaningful minutes in basketball are also the least valuable — and they still land in every average you read.
body: Here's a bar bet: when does a basketball team score most easily? The popular answer is when the game is already over — reserves running, nobody guarding, free points against a defense that has stopped caring. In 790 regular-season games of possession-level data, it is the opposite. Once a team's fourth-quarter lead passes 15 points — the cut this system already used, a hand-set line and not a fitted one — that team scores 105.34 per 100 possessions. The same quarter overall produces 112.51. Decided basketball runs 7.17 points per 100 BELOW the quarter it happens in, and no choice of threshold rescues the other answer: we measured 10 through 25 points and every one of them lands below the same baseline.

The interesting part is why, because it is not the defense. Shot quality in those possessions is indistinguishable from a close one: 48.77 eFG% with a big lead versus 49.68 for a team protecting a one-possession lead in the same quarter — less than a point apart (0.91), which is not a mechanism. What separates them is the free-throw line. A team nursing a small lead is fouled on purpose and shoots 0.493 free throws per field-goal attempt; a team up 15+ shoots 0.269. The close game is inflated by the foul game — garbage time is not starved of anything. The leader also slows down, 17.02 seconds a possession against 16.47, so the clock says the same thing the possession count does.

Why should you care? Because those points land in box scores wearing the same uniform as real ones. A bench player's hot line built at +24 is not the same evidence as the same line in a two-possession game, and season averages quietly launder the difference. It flatters certain profiles — deep reserves on great teams, volume scorers on bad ones — and it pollutes any stat that doesn't check the clock and the margin.

So do we fence it off? Not yet, and you should hear that from us rather than discover it. No player number on this site currently excludes these possessions: the 3890 decided-game possessions in this window — 13.5% of all fourth-quarter possessions — sit inside every rate we publish, the same as everyone else's. Building that fence is a real piece of work and it is on the list. Until it is built and live, claiming it would be the more comfortable sentence and the false one.
The next time a broadcast celebrates a 20-point night, ask the only question that matters: twenty points of what?

fence.note: A hand-set cut, and named as one. No fitted garbage-time boundary exists in this system; the sensitivity sweep below shows there is no behavioral wall to have fitted.

copy_fence.note: The fence the original copy chose. Measured on its own terms it agrees with the finding it contradicted.

index_row.one_line: A team leading by 15+ in the fourth scores 105.34 per 100 against a 112.51 baseline for the same quarter — identical shot quality, 7.17 fewer points.

method_note: Every possession is tagged by the ball-handling team's score margin at the moment it begins. Possessions estimated as attempts minus offensive rebounds plus turnovers plus 0.44x free-throw attempts; efficiency is points scored while a state held over possessions begun in it; eFG% counts a made field goal as a non-free-throw shooting play whose side's score advanced. Regular season only, exhibition and All-Star play excluded (1314 rows across 3 games removed by that filter). The 15-point cut is the one this system already used and is hand-set, not fitted.

provenance.note: This dive was published with its thesis reversed from the authored copy. Every figure on the page is computed by this builder from the warehouse at bake time; none is printed as written.
